function.name: patch
function.description:
Targeted find-and-replace edits in files. Use this instead of sed/awk in terminal. Uses fuzzy matching (9 strategies) so minor whitespace/indentation differences won't break it. Returns a unified diff. Auto-runs syntax checks after editing.

Replace mode (default): find a unique string and replace it.
Patch mode: apply V4A multi-file patches for bulk changes.

mode.description: Edit mode: 'replace' for targeted find-and-replace, 'patch' for V4A multi-file patches

path.description: File path to edit (required for 'replace' mode)

old_string.description: Text to find in the file (required for 'replace' mode). Must be unique in the file unless replace_all=true. Include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: Replacement text (required for 'replace' mode). Can be empty string to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false)

patch.description:
V4A format patch content (required for 'patch' mode). Format:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: path/to/file
@@ context hint @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
*** End Patch

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

target.description: 'content' searches inside file contents, 'files' searches for files by name

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits.

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file

Common questions about receiving medical treatment in China.

Is the quality of medical care in China comparable to Western countries?

Yes. Many Chinese hospitals serving international patients have JCI (Joint Commission International) accreditation — the same standard used to evaluate hospitals in the US and Europe. China's top hospitals invest heavily in state-of-the-art equipment, and their specialists often train at leading Western institutions. How much can I save by getting treatment in China?

Most treatments cost 60-80% less than in the United States, with comparable quality. A heart bypass that costs $100,000+ in the US typically runs $15,000-$40,000 in China. IVF cycles are $5,000-$12,000 versus $20,000-$40,000 in America. These savings apply even after factoring in travel, accommodation, and translation services.

Do doctors and nurses speak English?

The hospitals we partner with have dedicated international patient centers with English-speaking staff. Your assigned patient coordinator provides translation during all medical appointments. Many top surgeons and specialists have international training and publish in English-language journals. You should not experience language barriers during your treatment.

What happens if there are complications after the procedure?

All reputable hospitals we work with have rigorous safety protocols and emergency response systems. If complications arise during your hospital stay, they are addressed immediately at no additional cost. For issues that occur after discharge, we coordinate telemedicine follow-ups with your treating physician at no charge. We also help coordinate with your local doctor for any ongoing care needed at home.

How do I know which hospital is right for my condition?

Our medical team reviews your specific case, medical records, and preferences to recommend the most suitable hospitals and specialists. Absolutely. We encourage companions for most treatments — emotional support aids recovery. Companions receive the same visa invitation letters and can stay in the same or nearby accommodation. For major surgeries, having a companion is strongly recommended. Our coordinators can arrange companion travel packages and provide guidance on local activities for companions during treatment periods.

How long do I need to stay in China for treatment?

Stay duration varies by procedure: minor treatments may require 3-7 days, major surgeries typically require 2-4 weeks including initial recovery in the hospital and nearby accommodation. IVF cycles require 2-3 weeks for the full stimulation and transfer process. Cancer treatments like chemotherapy are scheduled in cycles. We provide detailed timelines with your treatment plan.

Is my medical information kept confidential?

Yes. All hospitals we partner with maintain strict patient confidentiality policies compliant with Chinese healthcare privacy laws. Your medical records, personal information, and treatment details are accessible only to your treating medical team and our coordination staff. We never share your information with third parties without your explicit consent.

What payment methods are accepted?

Most hospitals accept wire transfers, major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express), and some accept PayPal. Payment is typically made directly to the hospital upon arrival or before procedures. We do not take payments ourselves — all financial transactions are between you and the hospital. We can provide bank transfer guidance and receipt documentation for insurance purposes.

Will my health insurance cover treatment in China?

Most US and European insurance plans do not cover international medical treatment unless it's a life-threatening emergency. For self-pay patients, we can provide detailed medical documentation and receipts for you to submit for reimbursement or tax deduction purposes.
